## `chat_messages_search`

Class: read

Find Chat messages whose text contains a phrase. Google Chat has no search endpoint, so this reads recent messages newest first and matches the text here (case-insensitive). It scans one space (space) or the first spaces Google lists for the account, only messages newer than since (default: the last 30 days), and stops at maxMessagesPerSpace per space. The result says how many spaces and messages were scanned and whether a cap stopped the search, so "no matches" is never a claim about older messages. To go further back, pass an earlier since or a larger maxMessagesPerSpace.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | string | optional | Google account alias; "*" = all accounts; omit for the default account |
| `query` | string | required | Text to look for (case-insensitive substring) |
| `space` | string | optional | Limit the search to one space, format: spaces/{space} |
| `since` | string | optional | Only messages created after this RFC 3339 time, e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z (default: 30 days ago) |
| `maxSpaces` | integer | optional | How many spaces to scan when space is not given (1-25, default 10) |
| `maxMessagesPerSpace` | integer | optional | Newest messages to read per space (1-1000, default 200) |
| `limit` | integer | optional | Stop after this many matches (1-100, default 20) |
